title: What does a dog mean when it wags its tail
paragraphs: We all know what a dog means when it wags its tail – it means they’re happy, right? Well, maybe not according to leading animal psychologists who analyse what a dog may be or may not be feeling. There may be more of a tale in the movements of a dog’s tail than most of us think.

Most of us agree that it would probably make life whole lot easier and fun if dogs could actually converse rather than bark with us, but sadly they have not yet evolved to develop that skill. There are some obvious signs of what your pooch is thinking. For example, growling could show aggression, scratching at the door could mean a call of nature, and rolling on their backs could show submission. However, in the opinions of experts like Stanley Coren, professor of psychology at the University of British Colombia, your canine companion may be trying to tell you much more with the movements and position of their tails. For example, a broad wag is a friendly sign and can mean that the dog is pleased.

If you see the tail drooping, it may be a sign that the animal is in a state of stress and anxiety. That’s according to Josie F. Turner, a journalist specialised in animal welfare. This is especially obvious if there are whines coming from them, or they are trying to hide. It may be time to get them on the leash and take them for that precious ‘w-word’ – walkies. Most dog owners know never to say that word in the vicinity of their four-legged friend, or they will get overly excited forcing you to take them out.

A horizontal tail with slight movements may be a sign that your canine is nervous or uncomfortable. And the more ample the movements, the more nervous your pooch may be. Finally, an erect tail accompanied by a swagger in the hips and lots of movement is a sign that your dog is as happy as can be – and very alert. However, if the tail is straight up in the air with no movement, it could be a sign that your dog is alert and trying to exert dominance.

So, the next time you’re greeted by a dog, make sure to have a look and see what their tail is doing. In their own way, they’re trying to tell you if they’re sad, nervous or happy. Many of us would like to know exactly what they’re thinking. Maybe we should just be grateful their tails are wagging and they’re not plotting our demise.

vocabulary.entry: wag its tail /wæɡ ɪts teɪl/ 摇尾巴
vocabulary.example: The puppy wags its tail every time it sees its owner.
vocabulary.translation: 这只小狗每次见到主人都会摇尾巴。

vocabulary.entry: animal psychologist /ˈænɪml saɪˈkɒlədʒɪst/ 动物心理学家
vocabulary.example: The animal psychologist studies the behaviour of pets in different environments.
vocabulary.translation: 这位动物心理学家研究宠物在不同环境下的行为。

vocabulary.entry: converse /kənˈvɜːs/ v. 交谈；谈话
vocabulary.example: The two old friends conversed for hours about their childhood memories.
vocabulary.translation: 两位老友聊了好几个小时的童年往事。

vocabulary.entry: bark /bɑːk/ v. 吠叫；叫
vocabulary.example: The dog will bark loudly if a stranger approaches the house.
vocabulary.translation: 如果有陌生人靠近房子，这只狗就会大声吠叫。

vocabulary.entry: evolve /ɪˈvɒlv/ v. 进化；演变
vocabulary.example: Some species evolve over time to adapt to changing climates.
vocabulary.translation: 一些物种会随着时间进化，以适应变化的气候。

vocabulary.entry: pooch /puːtʃ/ n. 狗狗（口语）
vocabulary.example: My pooch loves to chase butterflies in the garden.
vocabulary.translation: 我的狗狗喜欢在花园里追蝴蝶。

vocabulary.entry: growl /ɡraʊl/ v. 低吼；咆哮
vocabulary.example: The dog starts to growl when it senses danger nearby.
vocabulary.translation: 狗狗察觉到附近有危险时，就会开始低吼。

vocabulary.entry: aggression /əˈɡreʃn/ n. 攻击性；侵略性
vocabulary.example: The trainer helps to reduce the dog's aggression through professional training.
vocabulary.translation: 驯犬师通过专业训练帮助减轻狗狗的攻击性。

vocabulary.entry: call of nature /kɔːl ɒv ˈneɪtʃə/ 上厕所的需求（婉辞）
vocabulary.example: The dog scratched the door, indicating a call of nature.
vocabulary.translation: 狗狗抓挠房门，示意要上厕所。

vocabulary.entry: submission /səbˈmɪʃn/ n. 顺从；屈服
vocabulary.example: The dog shows submission by lying down and lowering its head.
vocabulary.translation: 这只狗通过躺下并低下头来表示顺从。

vocabulary.entry: canine /ˈkeɪnaɪn/ adj. 犬的；犬科的
vocabulary.example: This park has a special area for canine activities.
vocabulary.translation: 这座公园有专门的犬类活动区域。

vocabulary.entry: broad wag /brɔːd wæɡ/ 大幅度摇尾巴
vocabulary.example: A broad wag of the tail suggests the dog is in a good mood.
vocabulary.translation: 大幅度摇尾巴说明狗狗心情不错。

vocabulary.entry: droop /druːp/ v. 下垂；耷拉
vocabulary.example: The dog's ears droop when it feels sad.
vocabulary.translation: 狗狗难过的时候，耳朵就会耷拉下来。

vocabulary.entry: stress and anxiety /stres ənd æŋˈzaɪəti/ 压力和焦虑
vocabulary.example: Loud noises can cause stress and anxiety in some dogs.
vocabulary.translation: 巨大的噪音会让一些狗狗产生压力和焦虑。

vocabulary.entry: whine /waɪn/ v. 呜咽；哀鸣
vocabulary.example: The puppy whines when it is left alone at home.
vocabulary.translation: 小狗被独自留在家时，就会低声呜咽。

vocabulary.entry: leash /liːʃ/ n. 牵引绳；狗绳
vocabulary.example: Please keep your dog on a leash when walking in public places.
vocabulary.translation: 在公共场所遛狗时，请给狗狗拴好牵引绳。

vocabulary.entry: walkies /ˈwɔːkiz/ n. 散步（口语，对狗而言）
vocabulary.example: As soon as I say "walkies", my dog runs to the door excitedly.
vocabulary.translation: 我一说“散步”，我的狗狗就兴奋地跑到门口。

vocabulary.entry: vicinity /vəˈsɪnəti/ n. 附近；周边地区
vocabulary.example: There is a small park in the vicinity of our neighbourhood.
vocabulary.translation: 我们小区附近有一个小公园。

vocabulary.entry: horizontal /ˌhɒrɪˈzɒntl/ adj. 水平的；横放的
vocabulary.example: The table has a horizontal surface that is perfect for placing books.
vocabulary.translation: 这张桌子的桌面是水平的，很适合放书。

vocabulary.entry: ample /ˈæmpl/ adj. 大幅度的；充足的
vocabulary.example: The dog's ample tail movements show it is very nervous.
vocabulary.translation: 狗狗大幅度的尾巴摆动说明它很紧张。

vocabulary.entry: erect /ɪˈrekt/ adj. 直立的；竖直的
vocabulary.example: The dog's tail stays erect when it is alert to its surroundings.
vocabulary.translation: 狗狗对周围环境保持警觉时，尾巴会竖起来。

vocabulary.entry: exert dominance /ɪɡˈzɜːt ˈdɒmɪnəns/ 彰显主导地位
vocabulary.example: The alpha dog tries to exert dominance over the other dogs in the pack.
vocabulary.translation: 这只领头犬试图在犬群中彰显自己的主导地位。

vocabulary.entry: alert /əˈlɜːt/ adj. 警觉的；警惕的
vocabulary.example: The guard dog remained alert all night to protect the house.
vocabulary.translation: 护卫犬整夜保持警觉，守护着房子。

vocabulary.entry: plot /plɒt/ v. 谋划；密谋
vocabulary.example: The villain plotted to steal the valuable diamond.
vocabulary.translation: 反派密谋偷走那颗珍贵的钻石。

vocabulary.entry: demise /dɪˈmaɪz/ n. 死亡；灭亡
vocabulary.example: The novel tells the story of the dynasty's demise.
vocabulary.translation: 这部小说讲述了这个王朝灭亡的故事。

sentences.english: We all know what a dog means when it wags its tail – it means they’re happy, right?
sentences.chinese: 我们都觉得狗狗摇尾巴就是开心的意思，对吧？

sentences.english: Well, maybe not according to leading animal psychologists who analyse what a dog may be or may not be feeling.
sentences.chinese: 但研究狗狗情绪的顶尖动物心理学家却表示，事情可能并非如此。

sentences.english: There may be more of a tale in the movements of a dog’s tail than most of us think.
sentences.chinese: 狗狗尾巴的摆动里，藏着的门道可能远比我们想象的要多。

sentences.english: Most of us agree that it would probably make life whole lot easier and fun if dogs could actually converse rather than bark with us, but sadly they have not yet evolved to develop that skill.
sentences.chinese: 想必大家都认同，要是狗狗能开口跟我们聊天，而不是只会汪汪叫，生活或许会轻松有趣得多。可惜的是，它们还没进化出这种能力。

sentences.english: There are some obvious signs of what your pooch is thinking.
sentences.chinese: 不过狗狗的一些想法，还是能通过明显的信号看出来。

sentences.english: For example, growling could show aggression, scratching at the door could mean a call of nature, and rolling on their backs could show submission.
sentences.chinese: 比如，低吼可能代表攻击性，抓门可能是想上厕所，翻身露肚皮则可能是表示顺从。

sentences.english: However, in the opinions of experts like Stanley Coren, professor of psychology at the University of British Colombia, your canine companion may be trying to tell you much more with the movements and position of their tails.
sentences.chinese: 但英属哥伦比亚大学心理学教授斯坦利·科伦等专家认为，狗狗的尾巴摆动方式和位置，可能还在向你传递更多信息。

sentences.english: For example, a broad wag is a friendly sign and can mean that the dog is pleased.
sentences.chinese: 比如，尾巴大幅度摇摆是友好的信号，说明狗狗很开心。

sentences.english: If you see the tail drooping, it may be a sign that the animal is in a state of stress and anxiety. That’s according to Josie F. Turner, a journalist specialised in animal welfare.
sentences.chinese: 专注于动物福利的记者乔西·F·特纳表示，要是狗狗的尾巴耷拉着，可能说明它正处于紧张焦虑的状态。

sentences.english: This is especially obvious if there are whines coming from them, or they are trying to hide.
sentences.chinese: 如果狗狗还伴有呜咽声，或是总想躲起来，那这种状态就更明显了。

sentences.english: It may be time to get them on the leash and take them for that precious ‘w-word’ – walkies.
sentences.chinese: 这时候或许该给它拴上牵引绳，带它去做那件重要的事——散步。

sentences.english: Most dog owners know never to say that word in the vicinity of their four-legged friend, or they will get overly excited forcing you to take them out.
sentences.chinese: 大多数养狗的人都知道，绝对不能在自家毛孩子面前说“散步”这个词，不然它们会兴奋得不行，缠着你带它出门。

sentences.english: A horizontal tail with slight movements may be a sign that your canine is nervous or uncomfortable.
sentences.chinese: 要是狗狗的尾巴平举，还微微晃动，可能说明它感到紧张或不自在。

sentences.english: And the more ample the movements, the more nervous your pooch may be.
sentences.chinese: 尾巴晃动的幅度越大，狗狗可能就越紧张。

sentences.english: Finally, an erect tail accompanied by a swagger in the hips and lots of movement is a sign that your dog is as happy as can be – and very alert.
sentences.chinese: 最后，尾巴竖得笔直，臀部还一扭一扭的，同时尾巴摆动频繁，这说明狗狗处于极度开心的状态，而且十分警觉。

sentences.english: However, if the tail is straight up in the air with no movement, it could be a sign that your dog is alert and trying to exert dominance.
sentences.chinese: 但如果尾巴笔直竖起却一动不动，那就可能是狗狗在保持警觉，并且试图彰显自己的主导地位。

sentences.english: So, the next time you’re greeted by a dog, make sure to have a look and see what their tail is doing.
sentences.chinese: 所以下次遇到狗狗和你打招呼时，记得留意一下它的尾巴动作。

sentences.english: In their own way, they’re trying to tell you if they’re sad, nervous or happy.
sentences.chinese: 狗狗正以自己的方式，告诉你它此刻是难过、紧张还是开心。

sentences.english: Many of us would like to know exactly what they’re thinking. Maybe we should just be grateful their tails are wagging and they’re not plotting our demise.
sentences.chinese: 我们很多人都想确切知道狗狗在想什么，但或许我们应该庆幸它们只是在摇尾巴，而不是在盘算着“算计”我们。
